title: The Opportunity Makers https://tntp.org/publication/the-opportunity-makers/
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), December 9, 2024 — original paper:
summary: Barton's page summarizes a TNTP report on seven high-performing public schools that reliably help students who start behind catch up academically, including students from historically marginalized groups. The report identifies three common factors behind these schools' success: a genuine sense of belonging, consistently high-quality instruction, and a coherent instructional program that ties subjects and activities together rather than leaving them as disconnected parts. Crucially, these schools focus on incremental growth for each individual student rather than short-window proficiency snapshots, and they use frequent, simple data checks to tailor support in real time. Intervention in these schools starts from grade-level content rather than watered-down material, with the same core curriculum often used for both mainstream and support instruction. The report offers this as evidence that significant, trajectory-changing academic gains are achievable without a perfect curriculum or ideal school conditions.
points: Trajectory-changing schools focus on incremental growth for each individual student over time rather than group proficiency in short testing windows, breaking large goals into celebrated smaller chunks.
Intervention should start from grade-level content with support layered on, not watered-down material; the same curriculum is often used for both core and support instruction.

Building genuine belonging is structural, not incidental: regular caregiver communication, advisory periods, and handoff routines between teachers reinforce that every student is known as an individual.

Significant academic gains are achievable without a perfect curriculum or ideal school conditions — the report's core claim is that relationships, consistency, and coherence matter more than a flawless setup.
quotes: This report from TNTP examines seven high-performing public schools that successfully help students catch up academically, even those from historically marginalized groups.

The study identifies three key factors contributing to these schools' success: fostering a sense of belonging, ensuring consistent high-quality instruction, and creating a coherent instructional program.
Rather than focusing on group proficiency in short testing windows, educators in trajectory-changing schools focus on incremental growth for each student.
In trajectory-changing schools, all students are given grade-level content, with support to access it if needed.
To create new paths of opportunity for young people, we must learn from what's already working.
